_meta.description: Roadmap data. Edit via scripts/roadmap_cli.py, not by hand. Run its `render` command afterward to update roadmap.html. Fully local, nothing here is ever pushed anywhere.

milestones.name: Fork and baseline
milestones.description: Fork the upstream extension, build it locally and confirm it works on Windows 11 with Zen Browser.
milestones.why: Everything else builds on a fork that is known to work on real hardware.

milestones.name: Theme modes
milestones.description: Light, Dark and Transparent themes for every website. Transparent has Partial and Full modes and a single transparency slider.
milestones.why: This is the core goal of the community edition: one generic solution instead of hand-written styles per website.

milestones.name: Zen interface sync
milestones.description: The transparency slider also drives the Zen interface (sidebar, toolbar, borders) through a companion userChrome.css.
milestones.why: A transparent page inside an opaque browser frame breaks the effect. Both have to move together.

milestones.name: Public site
milestones.description: Landing page, public Kanban board and roadmap on transparent-zen.vercel.app, plus a README with a clear disclaimer.
milestones.why: People need to find the project, understand that it is unofficial, and follow progress.

milestones.name: Release
milestones.description: Own add-on id, signed build and a public release that can be installed next to or instead of the official add-on.
milestones.why: The fork still uses the upstream add-on id, which blocks publishing it.

notes: This is a community edition of Transparent Zen. The official project lives at github.com/frostybiscuit/transparent-zen.
